clue.text: Composer has group leaving out middle piece

indicators.note: the central letter of the five-letter word for group is dropped

parts.note: a batch is a group of things made or handled together

explanation.surface: A musician's band carries on without one of its central members.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian Bach is one of the most famous composers of the Baroque era.

clue.text: Restricted diet born of a body that's not in good shape

indicators.note: the letters of these words are bent out of their proper form

explanation.surface: Someone out of condition placed on a limited eating plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Infants are fed a limited range of soft, simple food.

clue.text: Go away untroubled on holiday

parts.note: clear, as in a clear conscience, means free of worry
off work means on holiday

explanation.surface: A carefree person departs on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal order to leave.

clue.text: Material coming to us from space

definitions.meaning: worldly, unimaginative, tied to physical things rather than spiritual ones
heading towards our planet, as a returning spacecraft or meteor does

explanation.surface: Some substance arriving here from outer space, like a meteorite.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both bound for our planet and limited to worldly, material concerns.

clue.text: An ecologist denied new grant

parts.note: the indefinite article gives a single letter

indicators.note: the ecologist is refused the letter for new

parts.note: a Green is an environmentalist

explanation.surface: An environmental scientist was refused a fresh research grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grant' looks like a noun for money, but it is the verb meaning to concede.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a point is to concede or accept it.

clue.text: Drunk secure with line to walk on

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
to rope something is to secure it with a line

explanation.surface: A tipsy person fastens a cord to walk along.
explanation.definitionFit: A funambulist performs by walking along a taut cable high above the ground.

clue.text: Where one may stop getting on with noble family

parts.note: boarding a train or ship is getting on it
a house is an aristocratic dynasty, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: Somewhere a person might stay while rubbing along with aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop' here means to stay a while, as a lodger does.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodgers stay at such a place, paying for a room and meals.

clue.text: Universities working as one

parts.note: unis is short for universities
on means functioning, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: Colleges cooperating together.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things in unison means doing them together, simultaneously.

clue.text: Adding colour reportedly becoming less strong

indicators.note: says the word for weakening sounds like the answer when spoken

parts.note: dying, as a fading light or wind, is weakening

explanation.surface: Colouring something which is said to be fading.
explanation.definitionFit: To dye cloth is to colour it.

clue.text: Crashing bore very sensitive about conflict

indicators.note: the word bore is smashed up and its letters rearranged
the word for very sensitive is turned round

parts.note: raw skin or nerves are very sensitive

explanation.surface: A tedious person who goes on and on about some war.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boer Wars were conflicts fought by Britain in southern Africa around 1900.

clue.text: We nearly fed on plant, consumed with damaged skin

indicators.note: the word we loses its last letter

parts.note: to eat is to feed
a herb is a plant
eaten means consumed

explanation.surface: Some people grazing on vegetation, devoured and left with sore skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin long exposed to wind and sun becomes lined and roughened.

clue.text: Tangier reconstructed in stone

indicators.note: the city name is rebuilt, its letters put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Part of the Moroccan city of Tangier has been rebuilt using stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a hard igneous rock widely used as building stone.

clue.text: Heavens! Royal Mail has last word in fine computer systems

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: the postal and prayer pieces sit inside the fine and computer letters

parts.note: IT, information technology, covers computer systems
RM is the abbreviation for Royal Mail, the British postal service
amen is said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: An exclamation of dismay that the Post Office now controls the final say on IT.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens!' looks like an exclamation, but it is the definition, meaning the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of the sky, the heavens above.

clue.text: Depressed about river in flood

indicators.note: the word for depressed goes round the river letter

parts.note: feeling down means feeling depressed
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone feeling low about a river that has burst its banks.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown land is to submerge it, as a flood does.

clue.text: Started flying?

parts.note: literally lifted into the air, but the idiom means a project got going

explanation.surface: A question about whether something took to the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a venture getting started; literally it describes an aircraft taking off.

clue.text: Sponsor of moulded garden pot

indicators.note: clay of a pot is reshaped, so these letters take a new form

explanation.surface: Someone backing a pot shaped from clay for the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: At a baptism a godparent sponsors the child, promising religious guidance.

clue.text: Unpleasant quality of upper-class actor's part in G&S

indicators.note: the actor's words sit inside the two letters

parts.note: short for Gilbert and Sullivan, giving its two letters
an actor's lines are the words of the part

explanation.surface: A distasteful aspect of a posh actor's role in a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugliness is unattractiveness, an unpleasant characteristic.

clue.text: Single old woman endlessly frowning about legs

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the legs
the last letter of the word for frowning is cut

parts.note: stern means severe, with a frowning look
pins is slang for legs

explanation.surface: An unmarried elderly woman scowling ceaselessly about her legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinster was the traditional term for an unmarried woman, usually older.

clue.text: Girl with grand invested in old car to provide what's needed

parts.note: Bridget is a girl's name

indicators.note: the grand is placed inside the word for an old car

parts.note: a heap is slang for a decrepit old car
G is the abbreviation for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A young woman puts a thousand pounds into her old banger to get what she needs.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for an old, worn-out car.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to fill a shortfall, supplying what is missing.

clue.text: Okra, not European, to the back of one

indicators.note: the European letter is left out

parts.note: behind means at the back of
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A vegetable that is not from Europe is placed behind one person.
explanation.walkthrough: Bhindi is the Indian name for okra, common on curry-house menus.
explanation.definitionFit: The green pod known as ladies' fingers is called bhindi in Indian cooking.

clue.text: Soldier in wagon turned up suffering great distress

indicators.note: the soldier sits inside the reversed wagon
in a down clue the wagon word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cart is a wagon
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in an overturned wagon is in severe pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragic situation involves terrible sorrow or disaster.

clue.text: Drug user finally caught in Tube

indicators.note: that letter is trapped inside the word for tube

parts.note: a hose is a flexible tube

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word user is taken

explanation.surface: An addict at last arrested on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground railway, which makes the surface about an arrest on the train.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is slang for heroin.

clue.text: Two men in kingly legend

parts.note: the first of the pair of men is Arthur, a man's name
the second of the pair is Ian, another man's name

explanation.surface: A pair of men appear in a story about a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; the definition is adjectival, relating to the legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend of King Arthur and his knights is a famous royal myth.

clue.text: Spine damaged by stretching, needing input from hospital

indicators.note: the hospital letter goes into the word for ripped

parts.note: a torn muscle has been ripped by overstretching
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A back injury from overstretching needs hospital treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spine' suggests the backbone, but it means a prickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spine on a plant stem.

clue.text: Garment that's almost neckwear

parts.note: nigh means nearly, almost
a tie is worn round the neck

explanation.surface: An item of clothing that is not quite a scarf or collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, a garment worn in bed.

clue.text: Stuff material used to fill woven wreath

indicators.note: the stuffing of each word, all its letters but the outer ones, is taken

explanation.surface: Padding used to fill out a woven wreath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a noun for the padding, but it is a verb meaning to gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself is to eat far too much.

clue.text: Prompt to accept Conservative changing

indicators.note: the word for prompt takes in the abbreviation

parts.note: instant means prompt, immediate

explanation.surface: An urge to welcome a Tory who is switching sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconstant is fickle, always varying.

clue.text: Russian leader succeeded in turning informer

indicators.note: the S is placed inside the reversed informer
the word for informer is turned backwards

parts.note: a rat is slang for an informer
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A Russian ruler did well by becoming a police spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia before 1917.
